answer: Because the meadow deposit is held in the cedar escrow, the knoll audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases thus burns capital on every one it does not finish. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 90 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. The deposit is 18 dollars a seat. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
